title: Paul McCartney’s court hearing to dissolve The Beatles’ partnership – day four | 1971
content:
24 February 1971 was the fourth day of Paul McCartney’s court hearing to have The Beatles’ business partnership dissolved.

This was the first of two days in which a 46-page affidavit by Allen Klein, The Beatles’ business manager, was read out in London’s High Court. The statement was read by Morris Finer, QC, the barrister of John Lennon, George Harrison, and Ringo Starr.

The Beatles have not been prejudiced by my dealings, but on the contrary have greatly benefited by them. The assets of the Beatles partnership are in no way in jeopardy.
Allen Klein

Finer also presented a statement from accountant John Darby saying that Klein had increased The Beatles’ income from £850,667 to £4,383,509 during the 19 months since he had taken over at Apple Corps.
